extracted.intended_audience: International Preliminary Examining Authority examiners (IPEA), USPTO examiners handling PCT Chapter II work, and patent practitioners working with PCT Chapter II written opinions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing the written opinion and international preliminary examination report (Form PCT/IPEA/408) under PCT Chapter II, including searches, handling of amendments/rectifications, priority, unity, and the content/format of each Box on the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectifications of Obvious Mistakes (Rule 91) — marking and filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the IPEA authorizes a rectification of an obvious mistake under Rule 91, it shall: (i) indelibly mark, in the upper right-hand corner of each replacement sheet, the international application number and the date on which that sheet was received; (ii) indelibly mark, in the middle of the bottom margin of each replacement sheet, the words 'RECTIFIED SHEET (RULE 91)' or their equivalent in the language of the demand as well as an indication of the International Preliminary Examining Authority; (iii) indelibly mark on the letter containing the rectification or accompanying any replacement sheet the date on which that letter was received; (iv) keep in its files a copy of the letter containing the rectification or, when the rectification is contained in a replacement sheet, the replaced sheet, a copy of the letter accompanying the replacement sheet and a copy of the replacement sheet; (v) annex to the copy of the international preliminary examination report which is transmitted to the International Bureau any replacement sheet and any letter as provided for under Rule 70.16; (vi) annex to the copy of the international preliminary examination report which is transmitted to the applicant a copy of each replacement sheet and any letter as provided for under Rule 70.16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rectification is not taken into account pursuant to Rule 66.4 bis, use marking 'RECTIFIED SHEET (RULE 91) – NOT CONSIDERED FOR REPORT (Rule 66.4 bis)' when required; if unable to indicate non-consideration in the report, still follow marking/filing steps (i)-(iv) and forward replacement sheets/letters to the IB so elected Offices are notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner notation of mistakes and invitations to rectify
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the examiner is not responsible for discovering mistakes in the international application, if any mistakes come to the examiner’s attention they may be noted and called to the applicant’s attention. The examiner may invite applicant to rectify obvious mistakes using Form PCT/IPEA/411. Mistakes that are not obvious may be called to applicant’s attention in Box VII of PCT/IPEA/408.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PCT/IPEA/411 to invite rectification of obvious mistakes; use Box VII to identify non-obvious mistakes/defects in form or content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized officer signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PCT/IPEA/408 and Form PCT/IPEA/411 must be signed by an examiner having at least partial signatory authority. Form PCT/IPEA/420 must be signed by a TC Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every written opinion must be signed by an examiner having at least partial signatory authority (see § 1878.01 X).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of decision on rectification requests (Form PCT/IPEA/412)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant requests rectification of any obvious mistakes in the description, claims, or drawings, or in a correction thereon, or in an amendment under Article 19 or 34, the IPEA should notify applicant whether the rectification is authorized or refused using Form PCT/IPEA/412. Any rectification offered to the IPEA must be in the form of a replacement sheet and the letter accompanying the replacement sheet must draw attention to the differences between the replaced sheet and the replacement sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Space on the form may be limited; incorporate supplemental sheet(s) whenever necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listings handling during IPEA proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IPEA finds that the international application contains nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences required to be included in a sequence listing, the IPEA may invite the applicant to furnish such a sequence listing complying with the Administrative Instructions and pay a late furnishing fee (PCT Rule 13ter.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing Box I, indicate purpose for which sequence listing was filed (part of application or solely for search), time of filing/furnishing (filed on filing date or subsequently), and the format (paper, PDF image file, electronic Annex C/ST.25 text file). If multiple copies filed, indicate whether subsequent/additional copies are identical or do not go beyond the application as filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a written opinion must be established
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall receive at least one written opinion from the IPEA unless the Authority considers that all of the following are fulfilled: (i) the invention satisfies the criteria set forth in Article 33(1); (ii) the international application complies with the requirements of the Treaty and Regulations insofar as checked by that Authority; (iii) no observations are intended to be made under Article 35(2), last sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.484: IPEA will formulate a non‑binding opinion on novelty, inventive step (non‑obviousness), and industrial applicability; establish a written opinion if any defect exists or the claimed invention lacks novelty/inventive step/industrial applicability and set a non-extendable time limit for reply. ISA written opinion under Rule 43bis.1 is considered a written opinion of the IPEA for these purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ISA written opinion as the IPEA's first written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The written opinion established by the International Searching Authority shall be considered to be a written opinion of the IPEA for the purposes of Rule 66.2(a). The IPEA/US will consider the written opinion of the ISA to be the first written opinion of the IPEA and as such in most instances no further written opinion need be issued by the IPEA before establishment of the IPER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A further written opinion must be prepared if applicant files a response including a persuasive argument that the ISA written opinion was improper because of a negative opinion on novelty, inventive step or industrial applicability and which results in the examiner considering any claim to lack novelty/inventive step/industrial applicability based on new art not necessitated by any amendment. Such further written opinion should be established on Form PCT/IPEA/408. The IPEA may establish further written opinions under paragraph (f) of 37 CFR 1.484.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover sheet classification and cover-sheet markings
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing Form PCT/IPEA/408, classification of the subject matter inserted by the examiner in the header shall be either: (A) that given by the International Searching Authority under PCT Rule 43.3, if the examiner agrees; or (B) that which the examiner considers to be correct, if the examiner does not agree. Both IPC and CPC classification as required by the IPEA/US should be given. Since the IPEA/US considers the ISA written opinion to be the first written opinion, item 1 of the cover sheet is marked accordingly; the IPEA's written opinion must be indicated as a second opinion in item 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure accurate IPC/CPC coding and mark the cover sheet to reflect whether the ISA opinion is treated as first and the IPEA opinion as second.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-up searches (finding documents published/available after the ISR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA shall conduct a search ('top‑up search') to discover documents referred to in Rule 64 which have been published or have become available subsequent to the date on which the international search report was established, unless it considers such a search would serve no useful purpose. If situations in Article 34(3) or (4) or Rule 66.1(e) exist, the top‑up search shall cover only those parts of the international application that are the subject of international preliminary examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top‑up searches differ from additional searches (top‑up finds recently available prior art; additional searches respond to claim amendments). Perform top‑up searches in all Chapter II examinations except rare cases (e.g., subject matter not to be examined, claims so unclear/inadequately supported that no meaningful opinion can be formed, or no ISR for certain claims). If relevant documents discovered that lead to a new objection not necessitated by an amendment, issue a second written opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of opinion (Box I) — language, amendments, sequences, and new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: When completing Box No. I, item 1 of Form PCT/IPEA/408, the examiner must indicate whether the opinion has been established on the basis of the international application in the language in which it was filed or on a furnished translation. The opinion is established on the basis of any amendments, rectifications, priority and/or unity holdings and shall answer questions concerning novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability for each claim under examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List substitute/rectified/incorporated sheets as originally filed/furnished pages; indicate amended claims filed under Article 19 as amended; if opinion based on nucleotide/amino acid sequence, indicate purpose/time/format as described; itemize whether amendments cancelled any pages/claims/drawings/sequence listings; if amendments appear to go beyond original disclosure point this out in Box I item 4 and explain in Supplemental Box; new matter on a replacement sheet is disregarded for establishing the opinion but non-new-matter portions are considered; mark Box I item 5 if opinion takes into account rectification under Rule 91 and item 6 if it takes into account supplementary international search reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority (Box II) — treatment of priority documents and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the priority document is provided by the applicant after the preparation of the search report and the ISA written opinion, any written opinion of the IPEA and/or the IPER should reconsider the validity of the priority claim. The IPEA may request a copy of the priority document from the IB and, if necessary, a translation from the applicant. If outcome requires issuing an opinion without waiting for translation, issue opinion in the meantime and note under 'Additional observations' in Box No. II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the priority document is in a foreign language, invite applicant to furnish a translation within two months. Failure to furnish the copy or translation may result in establishing the written opinion and/or IPER as if the priority had not been claimed. Indicate boxes in item 1 of Box No. II appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-establishment of opinion (Box III) — when novelty/IS/IA cannot be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. III is intended to cover situations where some or all claims are so unclear or inadequately supported by the description that the question of novelty, inventive step (nonobviousness), and industrial applicability cannot be considered, or where the international application or claims relate to subject matter which does not require international preliminary examination, or where no international search report has been established for the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill Box No. III in accordance with instructions for Box No. III of Form PCT/ISA/237 (MPEP § 1845.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of unity of invention (Box IV) — notification and applicant responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. IV should be used to notify applicant that lack of unity of invention has been found. Subsection 1 indicates applicant's response to an invitation to restrict or pay additional fees: (a) applicant restricted claims to a group; (b) applicant paid additional fees for examination of additional inventions; (c) additional fees paid under protest; (d) (do not use); (e) applicant neither restricted nor paid additional fees. Subsection 2 is for when examiner finds lack of unity but chooses not to invite restriction or payment. Subsection 3 indicates which claims were the subject of international preliminary examination (all claims or identified claim numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims lack unity, issue invitation to pay further examination fees first and then perform top‑up search on inventions for which fees have been paid. Inventions paid for must not have been excluded from preliminary examination due to lack of international search in Chapter I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoned statement on novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability (Box V)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Box No. V, the examiner must list in summary form all claims with regard to the criteria of novelty (N), inventive step (IS), and industrial applicability (IA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application should be searched at least to the point of bringing the previous search up to date. Prior art discovered in a search and applied in a reasoned statement in Box V must be made of record in Box V. Prior art already cited on the ISR need not be re-cited. Subsequently discovered prior art must be cited in compliance with PCT Rule 43.5 and Administrative Instructions Section 503 using the same citation format as the ISR. One copy of each newly cited foreign patent document and NPL reference will be sent to the applicant and one copy retained for the application file; USPTO no longer mails paper copies of US patents/publications cited during international stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box VI — certain documents cited (types and citation practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. VI provides a manner of listing two types of documents newly discovered and not applied in Box V: (A) published applications or patents which would constitute prior art if published prior to the relevant date but were filed prior to or claimed priority earlier than the relevant date — list by application/patent number and publication/filing/priority dates; (B) non-written disclosure — list by kind of disclosure, date of disclosure and date of the written disclosure referring to the non-written disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite subsequently discovered prior art per PCT Rule 43.5 and Administrative Instructions Section 503 using same citation format used on the ISR. Include two copies of each newly cited foreign patent document and NPL reference in the Chapter II file sent to PCT Operations; send one copy to applicant and keep one copy for the Chapter II file. US practice: do not include paper copies of US patents/publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box VIII — observations on clarity and support
rubrics_metrics.description: In Box No. VIII, the examiner notifies the applicant of observations made as to the clarity of the claims, the description, the drawings, or on the question whether the claims are fully supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill Box No. VIII in accordance with the instructions for Box No. VIII of Form PCT/ISA/237 (MPEP § 1845.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Box VII — defects in the international application (form and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Box No. VII, defects in the form and content of the international application are identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill Box No. VII in accordance with instructions for Box No. VII of Form PCT/ISA/237 (MPEP § 1845.01). Use this box to call attention to formal defects and to non-obvious mistakes when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to reply to the written opinion (Box IX)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invitation by the IPEA to applicant to reply to the examiner’s written opinion will normally set a 2‑month time limit for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 1‑month time limit should be set when a 2‑month time limit would risk delaying establishment of the IPER beyond (A) 28 months from the priority date; or (B) 6 months from the time provided under PCT Rule 69.1 for the start of international preliminary examination; or (C) 6 months from the date of receipt by the IPEA of the translation furnished under PCT Rule 55.2. As a general rule set 1‑month where the written opinion has not been completed within 24 months following the application’s priority date. US rules do not provide for extension of time to reply to a written opinion (37 CFR 1.484(d)-(f) and MPEP § 1878.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art for written opinion and IPER (PCT Rule 64 definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Article 33(2)-(3) purposes, everything made available to the public anywhere in the world by means of written disclosure before the relevant date shall be considered prior art. Non-written disclosures (oral, use, exhibition) are not considered prior art unless evidenced by a written disclosure available on the same or later date; nevertheless the IPER shall call attention to such non-written disclosures. Published documents filed earlier but published on/after the relevant date are not prior art but must be called out in the IPER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant date is generally the international filing date (subject to priority rules): (i) the international filing date except as modified by (ii) and (iii); (ii) where priority is claimed and international filing date is within priority period, the earlier application's filing date unless the IPEA considers the priority claim invalid; (iii) where international filing date is later than expiration of priority period but within two months from that date, the earlier filing date unless the IPEA considers the priority claim invalid for reasons other than late filing. If a potentially relevant document was published between a claimed priority date and the international filing date, examine whether the priority claim is valid; for filings on/after April 1, 2007, priority should not be deemed invalid merely because the international filing was not before expiry of the priority period if filed within two months thereafter. Acknowledged prior art in the description should be regarded as correct and used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability as evaluation axes
rubrics_metrics.description: The international preliminary examination is conducted to formulate a non‑binding opinion as to whether the claimed invention has novelty, involves an inventive step (is non‑obvious) and is industrially applicable (PCT Article 33 and 37 CFR 1.484(a)). Novelty is defined in PCT Article 33(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Box V must contain a reasoned statement with respect to novelty (N), inventive step (IS), and industrial applicability (IA) for each claim under examination. Use prior art and top‑up search results as applicable.
